papers.title: The Bi-LF Positive Conjecture Holds
papers.abstract: We prove that a semidomain has length-factorial additive and multiplicative monoids if and only if it is isomorphic to the semiring of nonnegative integers or is a unique factorization domain. Consequently, bi-length-factoriality and bi-factoriality coincide for all semidomains, settling the Bi-LF Positive Conjecture. The main step shows that additive length-factoriality and multiplicative factoriality force additive factoriality, without an additive reducedness assumption. Multiplicative factoriality forces every semidomain with a nonzero additive unit to be a unique factorization domain. In the additively reduced case, a uniform multiplier for lattice points in a finitely generated cone yields cancellation of divisibility across sums, which leads to an obstruction to additive atoms dividing positive integers and completes the structural argument. We also consider related questions on quasi-factoriality and classify the rational and transcendental monogenic positive semirings whose multiplicative monoids are quasi-$n$-factorial for a prescribed integer $n \ge 2$.

papers.title: Modules with unbalanced support
papers.abstract: A finitely generated module has unbalanced support if its support has positive dimension but meets a top-dimensional component of the spectrum only at the closed point. We ask what homological signals are left behind by this geometry. Separating the spectrum into two wings, we prove first Tor nonvanishing for positive-depth modules and give criteria for second Tor nonvanishing. In depth zero, we obtain a structural sequence describing the finite-length torsion under a first Tor vanishing. A recent counterexample to the Peskine--Szpiro dimension inequality conjecture establishes the existence of modules of finite projective dimension and unbalanced support \cite{Ma}. We apply our framework to these modules and establish a numerical torsion--spine balance for linked Cohen--Macaulay wings. We also construct such modules over a reduced Gorenstein ring with exactly two irreducible components.

papers.title: Derived products and top-degree inverse limits
papers.abstract: We compute top derived products and inverse limits on products of affine lines with doubled origin over $B[s]$, for any nonzero commutative ring $B$. For every $B$-module $M$, the two top obstruction modules fit into an explicit exact sequence and contain $M^{\mathbb N}/M^{(\mathbb N)}$as a natural $B$-module direct summand.This gives exact product dimensions, sharp vanishing bounds for inverse sequences, and faithfulness in the coefficient module. For a Grothendieck category of finite product dimension, we also obtain degree shifts under adjoining commuting locally nilpotent endomorphisms and prove that this construction preserves top-degree vanishing for epimorphic inverse sequences. A fixed Gabriel--Popescu presentation then describes the general top obstruction through actual Ext sequences and separates two module-theoretic terms.

papers.title: Filtration theorems, Hilbert functions, and generic freeness
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a finitely generated module over a ring $R$ that is a finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring $A$ by $r$ elements. We prove that there are finitely many primes $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ of $A$ such that $M$ has a countable ascending filtration by finitely generated $A$-modules with the property that every factor $F_n$ has a filtration by cyclic modules of the form $A/P_i$, $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that the number of copies $H_i(n)$ of $A/P_i$ that occur in the filtration of $F_n$ is an eventually polynomial function of $n$. We prove a number of bounds on the degrees of these eventually polynomial functions: $r-1$ is always a bound, and the dimension of $\dim(M_P)-1$ is a bound under mild hypotheses. One application is an immediate proof Grothedieck's classic theorem on generic freeness. Several other applications are given.

papers.title: 2-nil Hyperideals of multiplicative hyperrings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the notion of 2-nil hyperideals of multiplicative hyperring.

papers.title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
papers.abstract: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.

papers.title: Reduction numbers under flat extensions
papers.abstract: The reduction number of the maximal ideal of a localization (or even faithfully flat extension) need not increase under specialization. Nevertheless, for each fixed local ring the reduction numbers of the maximal ideals of all its localization have a finite common bound.

papers.title: A Tropical Viewpoint on the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a tropical perspective on the recent arguments announced by OpenAI for Nagata's conjecture and the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture. By degenerating to both the normal cone and a semistable model whose dual graph is a cycle, we replace sections on a surface by Laurent polynomials in two variables. In place of theta functions, tropical methods bound the exponents of these Laurent polynomials, and a lift of the tropical Abel--Jacobi class of the normal bundle controls the shape of the resulting exponent diagram. Combining these support bounds with interpolation on a torus proves the Nagata--Biran--Szemberg conjecture with its predicted threshold whenever the corresponding linear series contains an integral curve whose only singularity is an ordinary node that is not a basepoint.

papers.title: The Fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra over nontrivially valued fields and the radius of convergence of nonarchimedean differential equations
papers.abstract: We prove a fundamental theorem for tropical partial differential equations, analogous to the fundamental theorem of tropical geometry in this context. We extend results from Aroca et al., Falkensteiner et al. and from Fink and Toghani for the case of trivial valuation as introduced by Grigoriev to differential equations with power series coefficients over any valued field. Crucial ingredients are the framework for tropical partial differential equations introduced by Giansiracusa and Mereta and a result on infinite intersections of projections of fibers of tropicalizations, which we prove using Hrushovski and Loeser's model-theoretic interpretation of Berkovich analytification. As a corollary of the fundamental theorem, we show that the radius of convergence of solutions of an ordinary differential equation over a nontrivially valued field can be computed tropically.

papers.title: The variety of orthogonal frames
papers.abstract: An orthogonal n-frame is an ordered set of n pairwise orthogonal vectors. The set of all orthogonal n-frames in a d-dimensional quadratic vector space is an algebraic variety V(d,n). In this paper, we investigate the singularities and components of the variety V(d,n), as well as the algebraic properties of the quadratic ideal I(d,n) generated by the orthogonality relations, which cuts out V(d,n) set-theoretically. By a general result of Ananyan and Hochster, these objects satisfy increasingly strong regularity conditions when d becomes large compared to n; we establish optimal effective bounds to quantify this behavior. We give criteria for the ideal I(d,n) to be prime or a complete intersection, thereby resolving open problems proposed by Conca and Welker. We give criteria for the variety V(d,n) to be normal or factorial. We provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture that I(d,n) defines V(d,n) scheme-theoretically. As applications, we improve the existing bounds for when the Lov\'asz-Saks-Schrijver ideals of simple graphs satisfy these four properties.

papers.title: Remarks on modules of finite projective dimension
papers.abstract: We investigate homological and depth-theoretic properties of finitely generated modules of finite projective dimension over Noetherian local rings. A central theme is the study of criteria for freeness and reflexivity derived from the torsion-freeness or reflexivity of tensor products of the form \( M \otimes_R M \) and \( M \otimes_R M^* \). Under mild homological assumptions, we prove that such properties of these tensor products impose strong structural constraints on \( M \), often forcing it to be free. These results generalize classical theorems of Auslander beyond the regular case. The second part of the paper is devoted to the dimension and support of Ext-modules, particularly \( \operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M, R) \) for critical values of \( i \), when \( M \) has finite projective dimension. We establish sharp bounds on their Krull dimensions, analyze their behavior for prime and equidimensional modules, and relate these findings to the grade conjecture and other homological conjectures, i.e., whenever $\operatorname{grade}(M) = \operatorname{ht}(\operatorname{Ann}(M))$ where Gdim$(M)<\infty$. We consider the problem that asks whenever is \( \pd_R(M \otimes_R N) = 1 \)? Applications include new cases of a question of Jorgensen, which asks whether \( \operatorname{pd}(M) < i \) whenever \( \operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M, M) = 0 \) and \( M \) has finite projective dimension over a complete intersection ring. Finally, we examine the projective dimension of prime ideals in rings that fail chain conditions.

papers.title: Asymptotic Resurgence of Facet and Stanley-Reisner ideals of Matroids
papers.abstract: Matroid configurations -- introduced by Geramita, Harbourne, Migliore, and Nagel -- are projective varieties which generalize so-called \textit{star configurations} and whose defining ideals are obtained by appropriately specializing the Stanley-Reisner ideal of a matroid. Motivated by this connection, we study the asymptotic resurgence of the Stanley-Reisner ideals of matroids. A result of Villareal shows that it is equivalent to study the asymptotic resurgence of facet ideals. We prove a formula for the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a matroid in terms of the Waldschmidt constant of facet ideals of the contractions of the matroid. As a consequence, we show that asymptotic resurgence respects the weak order on matroids of the same rank. Therefore, the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a given matroid is bounded above by the asymptotic resurgence of the facet ideal of a so-called \textit{almost-uniform} matroid of the same rank, which we compute explicitly. Guardo, Harbourne, and Van Tuyl showed that the asymptotic resurgence of an ideal is bounded below by the ratio of the initial degree of the ideal by its Waldschmidt constant. We prove that this lower bound is an equality for facet ideals of many classes of matroids, including matroids of rank $k$ on a ground set of size $n\ge 2k$ whose dual is paving, perfect matroid designs, and sparse paving matroids arising from Steiner systems. For the latter two classes, we explicitly compute the asymptotic resurgence.

papers.title: Pure dimension and counterexamples to the maximality of purely-primes
papers.abstract: In analogy with the notion of Krull dimension, for every commutative ring $R$, we introduce the notion of pure dimension $\pdim(R)$ by considering chains of purely-prime ideals. Then we see that the inequality $\pdim(R)\leqslant\dim(R)$ holds for a very broad class of rings $R$, including pseudo-Noetherian rings (e.g., Noetherian rings), Gelfand rings (e.g., local rings), mp-rings (e.g., integral domains), and rings with finitely many maximal ideals or finitely many minimal primes. In fact, for all of these rings $R$, we always have $\pdim(R)=0$, i.e., every purely-prime ideal of $R$ is purely-maximal. \\ However, we prove a classification theorem which states for each ordinal number $\Omega$ the proper pure ideals of the commutative ring $$R_{\Omega}=k[X_{\alpha} : \alpha <\Omega]/\big(X_{\alpha}(1-X_{\beta}) : \alpha<\beta<\Omega\big)$$ are exactly of the form $I_{\lambda}=(x_{\alpha}: \alpha<\lambda)$ with $\lambda=0$ or $\lambda\leqslant\Omega$ a limit ordinal (we write $x_{\alpha}$ for the image of $X_{\alpha}$ in $R_{\Omega}$). In addition, all of them are purely-prime ideals and form the following unique strictly ascending chain: $$I_{0}=0\subset I_{\omega}\subset I_{\omega\cdot2}\subset I_{\omega\cdot 3}\subset\ldots\subset I_{\omega\cdot\alpha}$$ where $\alpha$ is a unique ordinal with $\Omega=\omega\cdot\alpha+n$ and $n\in\omega$.
